title: A century in the making
text: In 1921 England's Football Association voted {{1}} ban women's football, on the grounds {{2}} the game was unsuitable for women — this at a time when women's matches were drawing tens of thousands. {{3}} took fifty years for the ban to be lifted, and {{4}} in 1993 did the women's game gain an official national league. The fight back since has been slow and then sudden: the Euro 2022 final at Wembley, {{5}} nearly ninety thousand attended, drew a bigger television audience than the men's final of the previous year. The sport {{6}} never looked back. {{7}} popularity is no longer a novelty but a fixture, {{8}} it took a century of stubborn players to build.

gaps.hint: conjunction: on the grounds ___ the game was
gaps.explanation: 'On the grounds that' — the fixed reason phrase.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ took fifty years for the ban
gaps.explanation: 'It took X for Y' — the fixed time frame.

gaps.hint: adverb: ___ in 1993 did the game gain
relative: Wembley, ___ nearly ninety thousand attended
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the final.

gaps.hint: auxiliary: the sport ___ never looked back
gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has never looked.

gaps.hint: possessive: ___ popularity is no longer a novelty
gaps.explanation: The popularity belongs to the sport: its popularity.

gaps.hint: conjunction: a fixture, ___ it took a century
gaps.explanation: The final clause is added: and.
